newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: PRESS DIGEST-CENTRAL AND EAST EUROPE-MARCH 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-CENTRAL AND EAST EUROPE-MARCH 3.

text.p: AUSTRIA
DER STANDARD
- Austrian government plans to clamp down on immigration, and drastically reduce the number of foreigners that will be allowed to enter the country. New laws are expected to come into force in July.

- Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger says a reform of Austria's tax system is unlikely to take place before the year 2000, says he wants to reduce the cost of labour while raising taxes on natural resources.
- Residents of Austrian state of Tyrol to vote in a referendum next week on whether their region should put in a bid to host the Olympic winter games in the year 2006.
- Connect Austria, an international consortium led by Austria's Radex, Germany's Viag and Norway's Telenor, plans to bid for Austria's third mobile phone license.
DIE PRESSE

- A joint offer by Raiffeisen Landesbank Oberoesterreich and industrialist Hannes Androsch's investment group for Austrian salt monopoly Salinen AG should be the winning bid, Landesbank chief Ludwig Scharinger said. The group bid a total of 750 million schillings for the company.
- Austrian state railways OeBB are increasing their efforts to attract a greater share of cargo traffic, railway chief Helmut Draxler says.
- European shipmakers have become the main customers for steelmaker Voest Alpine Stahl Linz, a unit of VA Stahl group.
KURIER
- The number of illegal immigrant workers in Austria has declined slightly over the past year, labour ministry says.
- Milchfrisch, the Austrian milk producers' central logistics company, will have to cut 400 jobs to enable it to finance a 200 million schilling restructuring plan.
- Austrian banks's cumulative operating earnings rose 7.3 percent over the past year, the central bank said.
ESTONIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- The police are still confused over a shoot-out in central Tallinn on Friday, when two men were injured. The shooter claims to have acted in self-defence.
- President Lennart Meri visited Sweden over the weekend and discussed the enlargement of NATO and the EU with Prime Minister Goran Persson.
SONUMILEHT
- Parliament social commission chairman said that pensions may rise by some 20-30 kroons in 1997 but the new law on pensions cannot come into effect yet.
- Estonian defence forces, border guard and Latvian volunteer defence organisation Zemessargi held an exercise in southern Estonia on February 26-March 2.
- MP Arvo Junti founded a new political organisation, the Association for New Policy.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- The hourly salary of highly qualified surgeons is 20-24 kroons. The monthly salary of a surgeon is less than 3,000 kroons while a GP receives 5,200 kroons.
- Prime minister candidate Mart Siimann decided to give up his share of a TV production firm due to a possible conflict of interests. The company began operating last year.

- Interior Minister Riivo Sinijarv met Russian Interior Minister Anatoli Kulikov in Moscow last week during an international conference on car thefts. A cooperation agreement between the ministries is being prepared.
POSTIMEES
- Siimann will begin negotiations on the new governmnet today with the Reform and Centre parties but has not yet disclosed his proposals.
- Former Soviet intelligence agent Oleg Gordiyevski warns Estonia against Russian intelligence in an interview.
ARIPAEV

- Finance ministry officials purchased large quantities of Union Bank shares while the commercial bank handles large funds of the state budget. The bank's management refused to comment if there was any connection.
- The price of Hansapank shares exceeded 200 kroons at the Tallinn stock exchange on Friday.
- Tallinn city government announced that no more loans will be made in 1997. Funds are sufficient both for the repayment of the Nomura loan and for investment.
LATVIA
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- On March 1 an armed gang held up a Latvian tourist coach on a road in Poland. One of travellers, Latvian Lizete Skudra, was shot dead.
- Hungarian President Arpad Goencz will arrive on official state visit to Latvia on March 7.
- On March 1 two rallies took place in central Riga to protests against the high cost of living and the ban on non-citizens taking part in local elections.
DIENA
- Latvia is likely to be admitted to the WTO by the end of this year after its legislation was brought into line with the organisation's requirements.
- The council of leading party Saimnieks on Saturday voted for the party's staying with the ruling coalition.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE

- A law on smoking restrictions comes into effect in Latvia as of March 1. There are serious doubts whether it will really work, since a ban on smoking in many public places, such as bars, restaurants etc. would ruin their owner.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- On March 6 and 7 Latvia will be visited by EU Commissioner Erkki Antero Liikkonen.
- Russian company Lukoil has received a letter from the Latvian authorities, asking if it wants to take part in the sale of the Ventspils oil terminal.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- Riga port rejected a draft agreement by the company Latvijas Naftas Terminals (LNT) to lease one of the harbour's quays. An agreement on building port facilities for common use, submitted by Neste and Statoil, was also rejected.
LITHUANIA
LIETUVOS RYTAS
- An to the Criminal code introduced by former interior minister Virgilijus Bulovas helped the notorious financial group EBSW to launder tens of million of litas, the newspaper alleges.
- Lithuania's national team will compete in group B with Israel, France and Slovenia in the European basketball chapionship in June.
- Lithuania might loose its oil transit business. Due to new customs documents regulations the transit of one oil tanker has gone up by 28 litas.
- The number of retired people is growing by 50,000 a year in Lithuania and in two years there will be more pensioners than working people.
RESPUBLIKA
- Deputy prosecutor general Arturas Paulauskas confirmed to the newspaper that he is considering being a candidate to the post of the country's president elections due at the end of this year.
- Lithuanian and Hungarian diplomats agreed on the text of a draft free-trade agreement.
- The collection of revenues to the state's budget has improved in February but was still below the target.
VERSLO ZINIOS
- From March 3 the newspaper will be published three times a week on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
- Lithuanian Gas told Russia's Gazprom that it will pay for its gas before March 10.
